purpose: Recheck impaired-network playback and pixel-latency validity after the received-throughput backoff fix
interpretation: All four cases pass the unchanged video, congestion-response, runtime, negotiation and lifecycle gates. These are fixed 720p30 trials with a 2–8 Mbit/s adaptive range, not the optional source-format ladder.

Direct delay/jitter/loss passes latency validity too. Baseline marker-to-expected-composition median/p95 are 56.602/57.559ms; the impaired phase is 104.893/122.817ms, with 0.276s freezes. This is one synthetic, same-host observation, not a physical capture/display measurement or general latency guarantee.

The other three cases fail clockAgreement, retaining their failed overall verdicts. Source capacity has a sustained wall/performance-clock offset change from about -1ms to -147ms during recovery (87 affected markers, 2.2ms maximum probe duration in those samples). Source impairment reaches 9.200ms offset and direct capacity reaches 7.800ms. Their full-run latency distributions are invalid and must not be published as valid bounds.

All four keep monotonic source markers. The older f654989 repeated pixel-stamp reversal is not reproduced in this series and remains a separate unresolved observation; the present sustained clock-offset failures do not explain that earlier event.

Do not loosen the 5ms clock gate or subtract offsets after the fact. Qualify a shared Linux monotonic timestamp and an explicitly bounded browser-clock calibration so wall-clock corrections do not contaminate duration measurement. Retain missing/negative/reversed markers and calibration failures as invalid evidence.

No pixel-probe, encoder, acceptance-gate or public configuration change was made between these cases. Whole-run resources include the qualification probe and do not establish its isolated cost or recording overhead.
